A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CamTrol, with the same authors, method and core contributions. All 23 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons, a user study, qualitative video-generation results and ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and reports additional complex-trajectory comparisons and a depth-optimization ablation.

M1.justification: The two-stage point-cloud modeling and noise-layout guidance procedure remains unchanged. Depth coefficient optimization already appears in v1, Equation (2); v2 adds an ablation of this component, not a new component. SVD was already a supported backbone.

E1.justification: v2 adds a substantial evaluation using camera trajectories extracted from RealEstate10k. v1's quantitative benchmark used eight basic motions with UCF-101 as reference, alongside qualitative complex-motion examples. That basic benchmark and the existing visual scenarios remain in v2.

E2.justification: Matching v1 Table 1's basic-trajectory comparison to v2 Table 3 preserves AnimateDiff, MotionCtrl and CameraCtrl; the qualitative comparisons also retain all three. The added complex-trajectory benchmark uses the existing MotionCtrl and CameraCtrl comparators, explicitly excluding unsupported AnimateDiff trajectories. No comparison algorithm is newly introduced or removed from the retained benchmark.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a primary comparison with a reported shared SVD backbone, 51 trajectories paired with 10 prompts each, and ParticleSFM-based ATE, RPE-T and RPE-R measurements. It also adds a 10-trajectory-by-10-prompt depth ablation and removes the 56-prompt human evaluation. The earlier 1,000-sample basic-trajectory benchmark remains in Appendix A.3.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4/Table 4 adds a focused comparison with and without depth coefficient optimization, testing its contribution to video quality and trajectory accuracy. Existing analyses of the base model, layout prior, timestep, backbone generalization and motion scale remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added tables continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty quantification.

E6.justification: v2 adds complex-trajectory and depth-ablation results and removes the human ratings. In the retained basic benchmark, AnimateDiff changes from 3699.34/65.81/11.61/0.3073 to 1582.93/73.79/13.39/0.3196 for FVD/FID/IS/CLIP-SIM; the other rows remain unchanged, making CamTrol best on FID. New Table 1 reports CamTrol ATE 3.917 versus MotionCtrl's 4.006 and CameraCtrl's 4.200. Its different backbone and trajectory setting prevent interpreting these new scores as same-setting changes from v1.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(5), including the depth optimization objective and diffusion equations, remain unchanged, as do the camera-motion definitions in Table 2. The added trajectory-metric descriptions introduce no new formal definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: training-free camera control through point-cloud modeling and noise-layout guidance, compatibility with multiple video backbones, and support for rotations, complex trajectories and varying motion scales.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the deformation-related FID caveat and discussion of comparable human-rated control with an interpretation of superior performance on complex trajectories. Appendix A.4 adds an explanation linking depth optimization to better view alignment. Its broad claim of trajectory-error benefits overlooks the reported RPE-R deterioration from 0.046 to 0.049.

D1.justification: v2 identifies ParticleSFM for trajectory estimation and explicitly specifies 25 steps for both inversion and generation. It removes v1's 16-frame, 256-by-256 specification and the user-study instructions and complete prompt list. The project-page access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the ParticleSFM citation to support trajectory estimation. The related-work section and principal novelty positioning remain unchanged; the existing RealEstate10k reference is merely renumbered.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the experimental settings and quantitative discussion, with smaller edits to ablation descriptions and the conclusion. The appendix removes the user-study section, adds depth optimization analysis and moves the other-backbone discussion from A.4 to A.5. The overall narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned around video quality and motion accuracy; the earlier basic-benchmark quality comparison is redisplayed as Table 3, and Table 4 adds the depth ablation. All 16 figures retain their visual content. Other changes are localized spacing, placement and pagination adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evaluation of the central camera-control claim through an explicitly shared SVD backbone, measured errors on real camera paths and a depth-optimization control. These provide a limited net improvement in experimental support. Benefits are tempered by removing human evaluation and implementation details, and by overstatements: Table 1 ties CameraCtrl on IS, while Table 4 shows slightly worse rotational error with optimization.
